An API key is a bearer token for an app, site, script or AI agent that calls your pod. It has two limits:

- Its **scopes** say which API surfaces it may call, one coarse gate per surface.
- Its **grant** says what it may touch there: kinds, actions, workspaces, projects or single objects.

A key can never do more than the person it acts for. Effective access is always *grant ∩ what you can see and do*.

---

## Creating a key

1. Open your pod's admin console (for example `https://pod-admin.example.com`) and go to **Keys**. A key for a
   single workspace is created from that workspace's **API keys** tab instead.
2. Click **New key** and name it after what will use it (for example "Portfolio site", "n8n").
3. Pick its scopes and its grant.

The key is shown **once**, so copy it immediately. Only a hash is stored.

For an AI agent, do not create a key by hand: `synap connect <agent>` (from `@synap-core/cli`) gives each agent its
own key and identity. See [Connect an agent](/docs/build/agents).

To create one programmatically, call the tRPC procedure `apiKeys.create`. `keyName`, `scope` (at least one) and
`grant` are required:

```json
{
  "keyName": "Portfolio site",
  "scope": ["hub-protocol.read"],
  "expiresInDays": 90,
  "grant": {
    "permissions": ["entity.portfolio.read", "document.read"],
    "workspaceIds": ["<workspace id>"],
    "label": "Portfolio site"
  }
}
```

---

## Grants: what a key may touch

A grant is a list of **permissions** plus optional **resource sets**. Permissions use the same keys as Synap's governance events, with an optional **kind** in the middle:

```
<subject>[.<kind>].<action>
```

| Permission | Allows |
|---|---|
| `*` | everything you can do (an explicit full-access key) |
| `entity` | every action on every entity |
| `entity.knowledge` | every action on `knowledge` entities |
| `entity.knowledge.read` | reading `knowledge` entities only |
| `entity.*.read` or `entity.read` | reading every kind |
| `entity.*.create` | creating any kind |
| `document.read` | reading documents |
| `view.read`, `project.read`, `session.read` | reading views, projects, sessions |

Matching is segment by segment. `*` stands for one segment, and a shorter permission covers everything under it: `entity.knowledge` covers `entity.knowledge.read` and `entity.knowledge.update`. There is no partial-word wildcard.

**Resource sets** narrow further. Leave a set out for no narrowing on that axis.

| Field | Narrows to |
|---|---|
| `workspaceIds` | those workspaces |
| `projectIds` | objects filed in those projects |
| `entityIds` | those exact objects |

How it is enforced:

- **Reads** are filtered in the pod's access layer, so a key with `entity.portfolio.read` never sees other kinds.
- **Writes** are checked at the governance gate before anything else. A write outside the grant is **refused**, never queued for approval.
- A grant **permits**, it never auto-approves. Agent writes still go through proposals as usual.
- A write that creates related objects (links, files) needs those subjects in the grant too.
- A key with no grant keeps the older behaviour: its scopes plus everything you can see.

### Doors a scoped key can read through

A key whose grant is narrower than `*` can only **read** through doors whose reads the grant actually bounds. Every other read door answers `403 GRANT_DOOR_UNSUPPORTED`;
doors are added as they are migrated.

| Surface | Read doors open to scoped keys |
|---|---|
| Hub REST (`/api/hub`) | `GET /users/me`, `/auth/status`, `/entities` (listing; a full-text `q` search is refused), `/users/{id}/entities`, `/entities/{id}`, `/entities/{id}/connections`, `/entities/{id}/facets`, `/documents/{id}`, `/documents/{id}/raw`, `/relations`, `/projects`, `/projects/{id}`, `/projects/{id}/digest`, `/projects/{id}/outputs`, `/tracks`, `/tracks/{id}`, `/views`, `/proposals`, `/channels`, `/threads`, `/threads/{id}/messages`, `/threads/{id}/branches`, `/messaging/channels`, `/messaging/linked-unread`, `/focus-sessions`, `/artifacts`, `/commands`, `/commands/{id}`, `/brand/kit`, and `/webhooks` (the key's own subscriptions) |
| MCP | `synap_get_entities`, `synap_get_document`, `synap_get_relations`, `synap_list_tracks`, `synap_resolve_identity`, `synap_get_project`, `synap_list_projects`, `synap_list_views` |
| tRPC bridge (`/api/hub/trpc`) | `entities.getEntities`, `documents.getDocument`, `relations.listRelations`, `relations.listRelationsPodWide`, `automations.listRuns`, `automations.getRun`, `commands.listCommands`, `commands.getCommand`, `views.listViews`, `proposals.listProposals` |

`GET /entities` without `q` and `GET /webhooks` are open to scoped keys on releases after v1.1.3.

Doors that combine several kinds of record (`POST /knowledge/search`, `/knowledge/ask`, `/knowledge/answer`,
`/entities/retrieve` and `/memory/search`, and MCP read tools such as `synap_ask`, `synap_orient` and `synap_find`)
cannot filter row by row yet. A scoped key passes one only when its grant reads every kind of record the door reads,
with no workspace, project or object limit. Every other read door (for example the REST graph, events and runs)
needs a key with the full-access `*` grant.

Writes go through to the governance gate, which applies the grant. On releases after v1.1.3, two kinds of write
need a key with unrestricted `*` (no workspace, project or object limit): doors that act on everything the person
owns and that no grant can narrow (for example the calendar feed URL, connector credentials and disconnection, and
deleting a vault secret), and, on the tRPC bridge, mutations the gate cannot bound yet.

### Access roles: reusable grants

Save a grant under a name in the Browser app (**Settings → AI → Access roles**), or with **Save as role** in any access editor. The next key, app or agent can start from it.

- A role is a **template**. A key made from a role keeps what the role said at that moment. Editing the role later never changes an existing key.
- The key remembers which role it came from. Pass `grant.roleId` when minting through the API; it must be one of your own roles.
- Only you can create or change your roles. Your agents can list them but never edit them.

### Limiting an agent

An agent's **capabilities** use the same permission keys. In the agent's panel, the same editor limits what it may **change**, down to one kind (`entity.knowledge.update`). An agent can always **read** what you can read, so the read column is shown on and locked. Leaving every box unticked makes the agent read-only. It never reverts to full access.

---

## Lifetime

`expiresInDays` sets how long a key lives:

| Value | Lifetime |
|---|---|
| omitted | **90 days** (the default) |
| a number (1–36500) | that many days |
| `null` | **never expires**. Choose this deliberately. |

Rotating a CLI key keeps its remaining lifetime.

---

## Key formats

The prefix tells you what kind of key it is:

| Prefix | Key |
|---|---|
| `synap_user_` | A personal key, created for you or for one workspace |
| `synap_hub_live_` | A service key (system-wide, or registered for a hub) on a production pod |
| `synap_hub_test_` | The same kind of service key on a pod not running in production mode |

## Scopes: which surfaces a key can call

| Scope | Gate |
|---|---|
| `hub-protocol.read` / `hub-protocol.write` | the Hub REST API (`/api/hub/*`), including its tRPC bridge (`/api/hub/trpc`) |
| `hub-protocol.admin` | treated as `hub-protocol.write` by every door; it only marks the key as privileged when it is created |
| `mcp.read` / `mcp.write` | the MCP endpoint (`/mcp`) |
| `data.read` / `data.write` | aliases of `hub-protocol.*`, honoured on `/mcp` only |
| `skills.invoke` | `/api/external/skills` |
| `chat.stream` | `/api/external/chat` and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint |
| `read:entities` / `write:entities` / `ai:analyze` | the n8n integration routes |
| `realtime:observe` | read-only realtime subscriptions |
| `providers.write` | AI provider configuration (operator tools only) |
| `setup.agent` | `POST /api/hub/setup/agent`, to provision agents on the pod |
| `probe` | marks writes as test probes, hidden from listings |

Older keys may still carry retired scopes (`preferences`, `notes`, `tasks`, …). No door ever checked them, and new keys cannot be minted with them.

---

## Workspace-bound keys

A key created for one workspace (from that workspace's settings, or with a `workspaceIds` grant) is **confined** to it. A request for another workspace is refused with `403`.

---

## Using a key

Pass it as a Bearer token:

```bash
curl https://pod.example.com/api/hub/entities \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer synap_user_..."
```

A key works on the Hub REST API, MCP and the other doors its scopes name. It does not work on `/trpc`, the endpoint
the SDK calls: that endpoint accepts only a sign-in session. See [SDK first query](/docs/build/sdk).

---

## Seeing and revoking keys

**My connections** (in the pod admin console's account menu) lists the keys you hold **and the keys your agents and apps hold for you**, and you can revoke either kind there. Each key shows what it may touch, e.g. "Read Portfolios, Documents · 1 Space". Revoking takes effect immediately: in-flight requests with that key get `401`.

---

## Security notes

- Keys are hashed at rest. The pod never stores the plaintext.
- An AI agent's key cannot mint keys for other agents, widen its own approval rules, or grant itself vault access. Those requests are refused or become proposals you approve.
- Keep keys in environment variables, one key per integration, with the smallest grant that works.
